map.基于5项临床与实验室指标评估肝硬化肝功能储备，用于预后判断和手术风险评估: Assess hepatic functional reserve in cirrhosis from 5 clinical and laboratory indicators, for prognosis and surgical risk assessment.
map.📖 查看「肝功能 Child-Pugh 分级（PT/INR 取高分）使用指南」: 📖 View the Liver Function Child-Pugh Grading (PT/INR higher score) Usage Guide
map.Child-Pugh 分级 = 胆红素 + 白蛋白 + 凝血酶原时间/INR +: Child-Pugh grade = sum of bilirubin + albumin + prothrombin time/INR + ascites + hepatic encephalopathy (each 1 to 3 points); 5–6 points grade A, 7–9 grade B, 10–15 grade C.
map.注：PT延长和INR任选一项评分，取较高分。原发性胆汁性胆管炎患者胆红素标准调整: Note: Score either PT prolongation or INR and take the higher one. For primary biliary cholangitis the bilirubin criteria are adjusted: 1 point <68, 2 points 68-170, 3 points >170.
map.：肝功能代偿良好，1年生存率100%，2年生存率85%。可耐受大多数手术。: : liver function well compensated, 1-year survival 100%, 2-year survival 85%. Tolerates most surgeries.
map.：肝功能中度受损，1年生存率80%，2年生存率60%。择期手术需谨慎评估。: : liver function moderately impaired, 1-year survival 80%, 2-year survival 60%. Elective surgery requires careful evaluation.
map.：肝功能失代偿，1年生存率45%，2年生存率35%。禁忌大型手术。: : liver function decompensated, 1-year survival 45%, 2-year survival 35%. Major surgery contraindicated.
map.提示：Child-Pugh分级常用于肝硬化预后评估、手术风险分层及TIPS适应症: Note: The Child-Pugh grade is commonly used for cirrhosis prognosis assessment, surgical risk stratification, and TIPS indication decisions. It works best when combined with the MELD score. For clinical reference only.
map.📚 深度解析：肝功能 Child-Pugh 分级（PT/INR 取高分）: 📚 Deep Dive: Liver Function Child-Pugh Grading (PT/INR higher score)
map.肝功能储备：由 5 项指标算分级，评估肝硬化严重程度: Hepatic functional reserve: compute the grade from 5 indicators to assess cirrhosis severity
map.手术禁忌：C 级提示失代偿，大手术风险高: Surgical contraindication: grade C indicates decompensation with high risk for major surgery
map.移植评估：反复 C 级或并发症者启动肝移植评估: Transplant evaluation: repeated grade C or complications warrant starting liver transplant evaluation
map.算法：总胆红素 >51→3、34~51→2、<34 μmol/L→1 分；白蛋白: Algorithm: total bilirubin >51→3, 34~51→2, <34 μmol/L→1 point; albumin <28→3, 28~35→2, >35 g/L→1 point; coagulation takes the higher of PT prolongation and INR (PT>6s→3, ≥4s→2, <4s→1; INR>2.3→3, ≥1.7→2, <1.7→1); ascites (none/small/moderate-severe) 1~3 points; hepatic encephalopathy (none/I-II/III-IV) 1~3 points. ≤6 points grade A, 7~9 points grade B, ≥10 points grade C.
map.例：总胆红素 35μmol/L（34~51→2分）、白蛋白 30g/L（28~3: Example: total bilirubin 35 μmol/L (34~51→2 points), albumin 30 g/L (28~35→2 points), PT prolongation 4s (≥4→2 points), INR 1.7 (≥1.7→2 points, higher score 2 taken), ascites 2 points, encephalopathy 2 points → total 10 points, grade C. If total bilirubin 20 μmol/L (<34→1 point), albumin 40 g/L (>35→1 point), PT 2s (<4→1 point), INR 1.2 (<1.7→1 point), ascites 1 point, encephalopathy 1 point → total 5 points, grade A, well compensated.
map.PT 延长和 INR 为什么要取较高分？: Why take the higher score of PT prolongation and INR?
map.PT 延长秒与 INR 都反映凝血功能障碍，但受检测条件影响各自波动。取二者中较: PT prolongation in seconds and INR both reflect coagulopathy, but each fluctuates under the influence of testing conditions. Taking the higher of the two avoids underestimating coagulation abnormalities, making the grading more conservative and safer, especially for borderline patients.
map.Child-Pugh 与 MELD 有什么区别？: What is the difference between Child-Pugh and MELD?
map.Child-Pugh 用 5 项临床/实验室指标，分级直观但主观项（腹水、脑病）: Child-Pugh uses 5 clinical/laboratory indicators; the grading is intuitive but subjective items (ascites, encephalopathy) vary by physician judgment. MELD uses creatinine, bilirubin, INR, and sodium, and is more suitable for end-stage liver disease queueing and short-term survival prediction. Clinically the two are often combined.
map.关于「肝功能Child-Pugh分级器」: About the Liver Function Child-Pugh Grading Tool
map.Child-Pugh肝功能分级器，根据胆红素、白蛋白、INR、腹水、肝性脑病五项: The Liver Function Child-Pugh grading tool assesses the hepatic functional reserve grade of cirrhosis patients from five indicators: bilirubin, albumin, INR, ascites, and hepatic encephalopathy. A professional medical tool based on authoritative medical standards, for reference only.
